chunks: Three: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ayub ibn Nuh, from some of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The naked one who has no garment, if he finds a pit, enters it and prostrates in it and bows. And what he mentioned after that regarding the manner of the funeral prayer for the deceased when he is naked indicates this, as narrated:

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ عَلَى الْمَيِّتِ: Funeral prayer (prayer performed over the deceased)
key_terms.حُفْرَة: Pit (a hole in the ground used for covering)

ai.seo_question: How should a naked person perform prostration and bowing if they have no clothes?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi cites this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the fiqh of *salat al-mayyit* for the naked deceased, establishing that entering a pit (*hufrah*) is a valid method for achieving the necessary modesty (*awrah*) coverage during prostration. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on practical adaptability in ritual purity and dress, ensuring the validity of prayer even when standard garments are unavailable, a principle directly extended to the funeral rites for the deceased.
